significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: an internal "representational transition" tracks a law's independently known "true boundary condition" and predicts the onset of extrapolation error or misplaced confidence, thereby constraining where outputs should fail across parameter sweeps rather than merely showing that a scientific concept is decodable. It establishes both a phenomenon—models differ between boundary-aware and "regime-agnostic" extrapolation—and a partial mechanism in which the encoded boundary signal is aligned with behavioral failure, although it does not claim that the signal causally controls predictions. Verified false is distinguishable and informative but weaker: it would rule out a broadly decodable boundary/error coupling in these models, not prove that domain knowledge is wholly absent; Ovadia et al. (NeurIPS 2019), which found uncertainty methods degrade under dataset shift, illustrates why a boundary-specific predictor rather than generic uncertainty is consequential. Topic-substitution self-check: the broad topic of scientific representations alone would not earn this score; the claim-specific boundary-location and error-onset relation is what raises it above the topic's obvious concept-probing hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Domain-of-Validity Score" combining "boundary-detectability, boundary-location accuracy, and error/boundary alignment," offered as a "read-only diagnostic that predicts confident-but-wrong extrapolation." It is potentially ex ante because an auditor can sweep a known regime boundary and flag unsafe extrapolation before relying on the model in that regime, although components based on observed prediction-error onset are post hoc validation rather than advance warning. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed relation still predicts that the recovered transition should track the physical boundary and error onset, but the submission explicitly limits the substantive findings as "law- and model-specific," so it does not provide universal numerical thresholds. Its asserted scope spans laws and foundation models in chemistry, physics, biology, and materials, with uptake by model auditors and deployers as well as interpretability researchers; the topic-substitution self-check therefore supports an above-median score because this specific audit handle and transferable alignment relation, not the scientific domain itself, create the reach.
